title: Why Story and Playtime Really Matter - Nautilus
gist: Most UK babies get daily screen time, averaging about 41 minutes a day at 9 months, while decades of evidence suggest infants learn language and social skills best through face-to-face interaction.

insights.claim: Most babies in the United Kingdom now get screen time daily, averaging about 41 minutes a day for 9-month-olds.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Quantifies early-childhood device exposure, relevant to children's media and edtech.
insights.locator: Most babies now get screen time daily

insights.claim: Infants learn language and social skills best through face-to-face interaction, shared attention and live conversational feedback with a caregiver, per decades of evidence.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Screen-based learning products face a developmental evidence headwind for the youngest users.
insights.locator: Infants are thought to learn best by doing

insights.claim: Differences in social engagement are a major feature of autism spectrum disorder and deficits there have been associated with slowed language development.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Links early social interaction to later developmental outcomes.
